title.narrative: UN-AU Partnership in Peace and Security II

description.narrative:
The project focuses on strengthening the collaboration between the United Nations (UN) and the African Union (AU) in conflict prevention, mediation, and peacebuilding. It aligns with the 2017 Joint UN-AU Framework for Enhanced Partnership in Peace and Security and supports the African Peace and Security and Governance Architectures (APSA-AGA). By enhancing the capacities and institutional frameworks of the AU and its member states, the project seeks to create sustainable improvements in conflict management and prevention.
Emphasizing the integration of the Women Peace and Security (WPS) and Youth Peace and Security (YPS) agendas, the project ensures their inclusion in all aspects of the UN-AU partnership. This holistic approach aims to promote gender equality, empower youth, and address the root causes of conflict. By fostering autonomy, establishing robust monitoring and evaluation systems, and ensuring necessary structures are in place, the project aims to achieve lasting positive impacts on peace and security in Africa.
Key outcomes for the project are as follows:
1. Strengthened joint UN-AU efforts in preventing and mediating conflict, sustaining peace, and addressing root causes of conflict. 2. Strengthened and structured partnership between the UN and AU for the management of conflict in Africa. 3. Strengthened capacity of the African Union to plan, manage, transition, and oversee AU Peace Support Operations, with a strong emphasis on civilian oversight, human rights compliance, and protection of civilians. 4. Integration of the Women Peace and Security Agenda (WPS) into all aspects of the implementation of the UN-AU partnership
